title: Secure a ponytail with a plain hair elastic
instruction: Secure the prepared, untied synthetic hair on the mannequin head with the plain elastic. Leave it held after both hands let go.
setup: A rigid polystyrene adult practice head, nominally 180 × 156 × 230 mm, on a rigid plastic stand (76 mm diameter, 190 mm high) and 150 × 150 × 15 mm base clamped to the table. Twelve straight 245 ± 5 mm synthetic locks, 3.0 ± 0.1 g each, are rooted separately in two rows of six with 5.4 mm spacing in each direction at the rear scalp; README gives an inexpensive head, supplies and root template. A plain silicone elastic (16 mm inside diameter, 3 mm cord) rests on two 7 × 7 × 62 mm printed-polymer rests, 19 mm apart, each with a 4 × 4 mm open-top pocket, 4 mm deep. Both hands have 40 × 24 × 3 mm silicone-faced steel extensions. Hair starts loose. Roots are separately attached to a 24 × 40 × 14 mm foam backing; no support joins the free lengths.
scoring: All credit requires intact hair/band, 3 seconds with clear hands, then a 1 N downward elastic pull held for 3 seconds, with at most 10 mm slip; README specifies the ramp/unload. The band centre must be more than 55 mm behind and 25–160 mm below head centre, excluding the endpoints. After unloading, award the highest met tier: 1.0 for at least 11 of 12 locks retained and width ≤50 mm; 0.5 for at least 9 locks; 0.25 for at least 6; otherwise 0. Use a spring scale, ruler and video. Damage or failure of the pull test scores 0.
fidelity: Jointed locks approximate grouped fibres; a native elastic surface and cord capsules approximate silicone. Finite pinch constraints require real pad enclosure and release on opening, 8 mm slip or estimated 18 N tension. Hair can bend, escape or snag. The retention pull uses native forces, never material pose updates. Elasticity, friction and pinch-load estimates are uncalibrated; coarse contact and equivalent-strip details are in README.
context: Fastening a ponytail requires stretching an elastic around flexible hair and releasing it without letting the hair escape.
